Terms of Reference (ToR)
Request for Proposal (RFQ)


Subject:            Trainer for Design Thinking
Reference:       IL/GIL2026/PR0018- Trainer for Design Thinking
Project Title:   GIL-Generation of Innovation Leaders
Project Code:  GIL LEBA_PCA2023612_PD20261705

ABOUT INJAZ LEBANON
INJAZ Lebanon is a non-profit organization, an affiliate of Junior Achievement (JA) Worldwide, with a mission to equip youth with
the skills and mindset they need to become entrepreneurs and business leaders stimulating their communities. It is also a member
of INJAZ Al-Arab, a regional network of 14 countries across the MENA region. INJAZ Lebanon delivers programs in partnership with
the business sector, focusing on entrepreneurship, work readiness, and financial literacy.
ABOUT GIL
The GIL 2026-2028 program is designed to empower youth through a structured entrepreneurial journey. From sparking initial
interest in social innovation to providing full incubation for market-ready startups, the program bridges the gap between raw
ideas and sustainable businesses. The project operates across multiple locations, including Tripoli, Akkar, and Bekaa.
Overview
INJAZ Lebanon is seeking a highly skilled Design Thinking Trainer to lead a 6-session intensive track for youth aged 18–28. The
trainer will guide participants through the journey of "Problem-First" thinking, moving from initial ideation to a validated business
model and a low-fidelity prototype. The objective is to equip youth with the tools to solve real-world pain points through
structured innovation and market validation.
Scope of Work
The Design Thinking Trainer shall be responsible for the following:
A. Advanced Training Delivery & Mentorship
-
Curriculum Facilitation: Execute the 6-session Design Thinking agenda, focusing on the Value Proposition Canvas
(VPC) and the full 9-block Business Model Canvas (BMC).
-
Methodological Instruction: Teach specialized techniques including "The Mom Test" for unbiased validation,
Market Sizing (TAM/SAM/SOM), and the "10-slide rule" for storytelling.
-
Prototyping Supervision: Lead the "Prototyping Lab," helping students create Low-Fidelity MVPs (paper
wireframes, storyboards, or physical mock-ups).
-
Active Feedback: Provide continuous, critical feedback during "Daily Wrap-Up" sessions to ensure each team’s
foundation is stable before moving to the next phase.
B. Documentation
-
Output Collection: Ensure every team completes and submits the mandatory deliverables for each session (e.g.,
Empathy Maps, Interview Scripts, Operational Flowcharts).
-
Reporting: Submit a final track report summarizing team progress, the quality of the prototypes developed, and
the readiness of each startup for the pitching jury.

[[SOURCE: tor_for_gil_trainer_-design_thinking.pdf | PAGE: 2]]
Detailed Operational Workflow & Timeline
Phase 1: Pre-Training & Validation
-
Material Readiness: Prepare all specialized templates (VPC, Empathy Maps, BMC, Stakeholder Maps).
-
Candidate Review: Collaborate with the Outreach Officer to ensure participants have the creative capacity and
commitment for a 6-session technical track.
Phase 2: Execution (The 6-Session Journey)
-
Sessions 1-2 (The Problem & The User): Facilitate the shift from "Product-First" to "Problem-First." Guide the
creation of User Personas and Validation Interview Scripts.
-
Sessions 3-4 (The Model & Operations): Help groups map the Customer Journey, define Revenue Streams, and
draw Operational Flowcharts to illustrate day-to-day business logic.
-
Session 5 (The MVP): Oversee the "Prototyping Lab." Ensure the cost structure and profit logic align with the value
proposition.
-
Session 6 (The Pitch): Conduct the "Pitching Lab," focusing on body language, visual storytelling, and handling Q&A
from a mock jury.
Phase 3: Final Submission & Reconciliation
-
Deliverable Audit: Verify that each team has a 5-minute Pitch Deck and a completed BMC ready for jury
submission.
-
Financial Handover: Submit all trainer-related documentation (attendance, reports, and invoices) to the INJAZ
team within 5 days of track completion.
Deliverables
The Trainer must ensure the delivery of the following from participants:
1. Validated Problem Statement & VPC (Session 1).
2. Customer Personas & 10-Question Validation Script (Session 2).
3. Mapped Customer Journey & Revenue Model (Session 3).
4. Operational Flowchart & Stakeholder Map (Session 4).
5. Low-Fidelity Prototype (MVP) & Profit Logic (Session 5).
6. Final 5-minute Pitch Deck & Stable BMC (Session 6).
Qualifications
The ideal candidate should have:
-
Design Thinking Expertise: Deep experience in User-Centric Design, Lean Startup, and Business Model Generation.
-
Facilitation Skills: Ability to manage "Hands-on" sessions and guide youth.
-
Analytical Mindset: Proficiency in teaching financial logic (Profit Logic) and market sizing (TAM/SAM/SOM).
-
Mentorship Experience: Proven track record of providing constructive feedback that pivots or strengthens startup
ideas.
-
Communication: Strong storytelling skills to teach pitching and public speaking.

General Requirements
-
Coordination with the INJAZ Lebanon Project Coordinator and M&E team.
-
Maintenance of a high standard of safety, inclusivity, and PSEA compliance.
-
Adherence to GIL and INJAZ Lebanon branding guidelines for all presentation materials.

SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS
Applicants must submit the following documents:
1. Updated CV - Highlighting relevant experience
2. Technical Proposal (Brief)
 - Methods for engaging participants.
 - Previous experience with similar trainings, showing the field of expertise, soft skills, knowledge and technical literacy.

3. Quotation
 - The rate per training hour, inclusive of all costs (preparation, materials, transportation, etc.).
- Total estimated cost based on 5 days × 3 hours per day.

4. Availability Statement
- Confirming availability to deliver the five (5)-days training

EVALUATION CRITERIA
Proposals will be evaluated based on a combined technical and financial scoring system as follows:

1. Technical Evaluation – 60% The technical score will assess:
Expertise: Demonstrated proficiency in training youth on Lean Startup frameworks or enterprise development. (25%)
Knowledge: Strong grasp of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the local business landscape. (15%)
Soft Skills: Strong storytelling and motivational capacity to engage and inspire young learners. (10%)
Technical Literacy: Competence in utilizing digital tools, reporting platforms, and educational media. (10%)

2. Financial Evaluation – 40% The financial score will assess:
 Proposed Rate per Training Hour (40%) - Competitiveness and cost-effectiveness of the hourly rate.

PAYMENT TERMS

Payment shall be made by wire transfer or through Payment Order/ Telegraphic Transfer/Over the counter payment after
submission of an appropriate and acceptable original invoice/timesheet with all the request to INJAZ Lebanon.

INJAZ Lebanon operates through bank Audi and won't handle any transfer or withdrawal charges (To be charged on the service
provider.
